newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $71 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle market quiet, bid $71 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were at $71.00 per cwt amid moderate inquiry, with asking levels at $72.00 to $73.00, they said.
Feedlot managers continued to look for $72.00 trades either later Tuesday or Wednesday, which would be up $1.00 from Monday's light activity.
Prices were expected to be underpinned by tight supplies of high yield cattle and by expectations for continued moderate to strong beef demand, the feedlot sources said.
Beef demand was expected to be fueled by late retail buying for pre-Thanksgiving beef features, market sources said. Early orders for post-holiday features could also buoy the beef market, they said.
Gains in choice graded cuts were expected to continue outpacing select grades because of the tight supply of choice graded cattle.
